commit.message:
Add error boundary around the PostDetailPage kind dispatch

The detail page reached by /naddr1... has its own kind-based content
switch (PostDetailPage.tsx:2238-2353) that mirrors the one in NoteCard.
A renderer that throws inside it (e.g. a broken article, a malformed
Zapstore release, a custom-NIP card from a lazy chunk) used to bubble
up to the new center-column boundary and blank out the entire route.

Wrapping just the ContentWarningGuard kind-dispatch in an inline
ErrorBoundary mirrors the NoteCard treatment: the author header,
comment context, stats row, and PostActionBar (reply / repost / zap)
stay interactive, and the broken body is replaced with the same
BrokenEventFallback tombstone used in feeds. resetKeys=[event.id]
means navigating to a different event recovers without a reload.

commit.message:
Add error boundary around the center column

A page-level render error (e.g. a route handler that throws while
processing a malformed naddr) used to bubble all the way to the
top-level boundary in main.tsx, blanking out the sidebar, mobile top
bar, and mobile bottom nav along with the broken content. Wrapping
just the <Outlet /> in an ErrorBoundary keeps the rest of the shell
interactive so the user can navigate elsewhere via the sidebar.

resetKeys=[location.pathname] re-mounts the boundary on every route
change, so navigating away from a broken URL recovers without a page
reload.

commit.message:
Add per-item error boundaries to feeds and embedded events

A malformed event whose renderer throws (e.g. an unguarded nip19 encode
on attacker-controlled tag data) used to take down the entire feed,
detail page, or profile pinned-posts list, leaving the user with only
the top-level full-page fallback. Now each NoteCard's kind-dispatched
content block and each EmbeddedNote / EmbeddedNaddr render in their own
error boundary, so one broken event is replaced with a small tombstone
('This post could not be displayed') and the surrounding feed/card keeps
working.

Migrates the existing in-house ErrorBoundary onto react-error-boundary
to gain a render-prop fallback and resetKeys without losing the existing
public API or Sentry reporting. Per-item boundaries report at level
'error' (vs. 'fatal' for the top-level boundary) with a tag identifying
the placement (note-card / embedded-note / embedded-naddr) so they can
be triaged separately from app-wide crashes.

commit.message:
Extract parseAddr utility for kind:pubkey:identifier coordinates

The previous commit added a private parseAddr helper inside HighlightContent
but didn't use it for the ~10 other sites that split A-tag values the same
way — most notably parseCommentRoot, which open-coded the exact same logic.

Hoist parseAddr (with the validated-pubkey postcondition) to
src/lib/parseAddr.ts and route every kind:pubkey:identifier split through
it: parseCommentRoot, parseProfileBadges, parseBadgeSet, parseBadgeATag,
usePendingBadges, ProfilePage's badge ref extraction, PostDetailPage's
profile/community/generic addr roots and root-event reconstruction,
ComposeBox's root-event reconstruction, AppHandlerContent's
Shakespeare/nsite ref extraction, useCustomEmojis' emoji-pack refs, and
the local parseATagRef in usePlaylistTracks/usePlaylistCoverArt. The
playlist hooks and ProfilePage previously had no hex validation at all —
they now reject malformed pubkeys at parse time like every other site.

Tests cover the well-formed case, empty d-tag, d-tags containing colons,
short/non-numeric/malformed inputs, and the length-9 hex crash repro.

commit.message:
Harden nip19 encode call sites against malformed hex inputs

A kind 10008/30008 profile-badges event with a malformed pubkey in one of its
`a` tag references would crash the entire NoteCard tree with 'padded hex
string expected, got unpadded hex of length N' from @noble/hashes deep
inside nip19.naddrEncode. The same bug class affected PeopleAvatarStack,
ReplyContext, ParticipantRow, zap sender rows, comment context, and ~10
other components — anywhere a pubkey or event id was extracted from event
tag content and passed to a nip19 encoder without hex validation.

Establish validity of pubkeys/event-ids as a parse-layer precondition, not
a render-time concern, and make it hard to reintroduce the bug class.

- Add isNostrId() in src/lib/nostrId.ts backed by Nostrify's NSchema.id(),
  branded as a HexId type guard so TypeScript narrows callers in the true
  branch while leaving the false branch untouched. HexId is assignable to
  string everywhere; no runtime cost.
- Add non-throwing tryNpubEncode / tryNeventEncode / tryNaddrEncode /
  tryNoteEncode / tryNprofileEncode wrappers in src/lib/safeNip19.ts.
- encodeEvent.ts returns the precise nostr-tools template-literal types
  (NPub, NEvent, NAddr) instead of plain `string`, so leaf components
  that take an encoded identifier as a prop can declare it as NPub/NEvent/
  NAddr and the compiler rejects a raw hex string at the call site instead
  of failing at runtime inside @noble/hashes. Add encodeEventNpub(event)
  so the very common `nip19.npubEncode(event.pubkey)` pattern has a
  typed wrapper.
- nostrIdentifier.ts's tryDecodeNip19 and detectIdentifier carry
  NPub/NProfile/Note/NEvent/NAddr on their `raw` fields per variant, so
  downstream consumers (search, NIP-19 router) can pass those values
  straight through without re-typing or re-encoding.
- Filter at every parse layer: parseProfileBadges, parsePeopleList,
  parseCommentRoot, parseLetterEvent, parseParticipants, parseGeocacheAddr,
  parseAddr (highlights), usePendingBadges, follow/curator/user-list hooks,
  getBadgeRecipients, extractZapSender, PostDetailPage A-tag splits, and
  useMuteList's normalisers (which now return undefined on failure instead
  of silently passing garbage through).
- Sweep inline /^[0-9a-f]{64}$/i checks at parse layers (useStreamPosts,
  useNip05Resolve, usePostComment, useMuteList, weatherStation,
  parseBadgeSet, parseProfileBadges, schemas) and replace with isNostrId.
  The /i flag was a long-standing bug — uppercase hex is never valid in
  Nostr and NSchema.id() rejects it. The pre-existing mute-list normaliser
  depended on the /i tolerance to lowercase SHOUTING input; that codepath
  was already untested and is now removed along with the regex.
- Renderers operate on already-validated data and use plain nip19 encoders.
- Tests for isNostrId, safeNip19 wrappers, and parsePeopleList's
  drop-malformed-p-tag behaviour (regression for the PeopleAvatarStack
  crash).
